title: First Thing: Peltola’s Alaska victory secures 56th Democratic seat in Senate
summary:
The ninth gain of the midterms in the upper chamber, it is the first time Alaska has elected a Democrat since 2008. Plus the impact the NAZA documentary is having inside Israel

Good morning.…

blocks.text: Good morning. Democrats will control 56 seats in the upper chamber after the final Senate race was called in favor of Mary Peltola. The party gained nine Senate seats in the midterms, a sweeping victory that will put them decisively back in the majority beginning next year. Peltola, a former US House lawmaker, is the first Democrat Alaska has elected to the Senate since 2008.

Her campaign was dogged by controversy after the New York Times reported her staffers had helped recruit a second Republican challenger also named Dan Sullivan to run. Although Peltola’s team denied involvement, the alleged ruse prompted Donald Trump to call for her prosecution and triggered federal and state investigations.
National Security Agency network for internal communications goes down

The US National Security Agency said on Tuesday it had experienced “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after reports that its classified internal communications network had gone down. In a statement, the agency said some internal systems were affected but “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational”.

The outage follows a run of technology failures in recent days, including a nationwide ground stop of flights, a Microsoft outage and disruption to banking services. None of those have been tied to a cyber-attack, though the causes of some have not been fully explained.

items: What has Marco Rubio said about the series of tech failures? The US secretary of state said: “We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind.”

Where have JD Vance and Sean Duffy tried to apportion blame? In separate interviews the vice-president and the transportation secretary have bizarrely tried to link Friday’s flight stoppage with transgender issues.

blocks.text: Biden criticizes Zelenskyy as ‘moody’ and ‘not as grateful as I expected’ in new memoir

blocks.caption: Joe Biden in a bilateral meeting with the president of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Photograph: The Washington Post/Getty Images

blocks.text: In a new memoir, Joe Biden offers harsh criticism of Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has led Ukraine through four and a half years of war against Russia. According to Biden, the Ukrainian president was “difficult to work with”, “moody and stubborn in our private conversations”, and “not as grateful as I expected” for US diplomatic support and military aid.

items: How did Ukraine pull off the attack on the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule? Luke Harding reports from Kyiv on the in-depth preparations Ukraine made before launching a wave of attacks against the bridge that links Russia with occupied Crimea, personally opened by the Russian president in 2018.

How is Kyiv coping with continued Russian strikes? Many homes in Ukraine’s capital only have power for four hours a day, well before the winter months when freezing temperatures will put far more strain on infrastructure. Andrew Roth reports that many are beginning to blame the city’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, for failing to prepare.

blocks.text: Man armed with axe accused of destroying US military plane at Shannon airport in Ireland

blocks.caption: A US military C-130H aircraft. Photograph: US Department of Justice/PA

blocks.text: An axe-wielding man breached a security perimeter and destroyed an American military plane while it was parked at an Irish airport, US prosecutors claimed. Daithi O’Corrain, 48, is accused of cutting hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit gauges and pouring ball bearings into fuel tanks during the incident in April. He is not in US custody and his arraignment on the charge has not been scheduled.
Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang

blocks.caption: The former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Photograph: Ann Wang/Reuters

blocks.text: Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chair of the company’s board said during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster. Nvidia announced its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The announcement comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life

blocks.caption: Young Awá men seen in 2017. Photograph: Scott Wallace/Getty Images

blocks.text: About 20 members of the uncontacted Awá Indigenous group emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, entering a village. Local people offered food to the group, who asked for yams before returning to the forest. With local Indigenous leaders warning of “clear signs of severe emaciation” among the children and elderly Awá, rights groups said the rare contact raised alarm over increasing incursions by illegal loggers, hunters and cattle ranchers into their territory.
In other news …

blocks.caption: Asif Merchant, a Pakistani man with alleged ties to Iran, appears on charges in connection with a foiled plot to assassinate Trump. Photograph: Jane Rosenberg/Reuters

items: A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of the Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani.

An eight-year-old Haitian boy has returned home to California after being released from ICE custody. The third-grader was put in restraints and taken into custody and held in Texas after a check-in earlier in the month.
The Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodríguez has been shot dead. He had gained prominence for publishing allegations against ⁠suspected drug traffickers and politicians.

California prosecutors and victims’ advocates have sued the state’s governor to stop him from commuting death sentences. Gavin Newsom’s mass clemency action would leave all 548 people facing execution in the state instead facing life sentences without the possibility of parole.
The US has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, global health authorities announced.
Amazon’s founder and billionaire chair Jeff Bezos has said he was “heavily involved” in the decision to cast Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.

blocks.text: Stat of the day: US Pentagon fails ninth straight audit

blocks.caption: The Pentagon. Photograph: Kevin Carter/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Pentagon failed a financial audit for the ninth consecutive year, according to an inspector general ⁠report – but an official said a majority of its units passed for the first time.
Well Actually: An A-Z of how to eat plants in full – for extra flavor, fiber and savings

blocks.caption: Eat all of your veg.  Composite: Guardian design;  Norman Posselt; Creativ Studio Heinemann; Jessica Peterson; Charles Wollertz/Getty Images

blocks.text: If you discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds when consuming fruit and vegetables you are missing out on a lot of value. Rachel Dixon has this comprehensive guide of what to incorporate into your diet – and what to avoid.
Don’t miss this: ‘They want silence’: how the film NAZA is shaking Israel

blocks.caption: A mural in Israel initially targeting the directors of the NAZA documentary has been altered to read ‘heroes’ instead of ‘traitors’. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: The film’s material is shocking – it details the secret systems that have left tens of thousands of civilians dead and millions more homeless, displaced and injured in Gaza. Michael Segalov examines its impact within Israel.
Climate check: Fossil-fuel industry accused of violating Colorado law over not disclosing drilling chemicals

blocks.caption: Crews work at an oil and gas rig in Weld County, Colorado. Photograph: RJ Sangosti/The Denver Post via Getty Images

blocks.text: The fossil-fuel industry is violating Colorado law by not disclosing which chemicals it uses in drilling, a new analysis by the FracTracker Alliance non-profit alleges, and state records show it has used illegal or dangerous compounds while fracking.

items: Follow the latest from Cop31 with Ajit Niranjan on our live blog.

blocks.text: Last Thing: US libraries see rise in visitors as patrons seek affordable resources

blocks.caption: The central building of the Brooklyn Public Library. Photograph: Roy Rochlin/Getty Images

blocks.text: Inflation and expanding services are drawing more people to public libraries, which are offering everything from books to job support and free activities.
